assessment.nobel_worthiness: A genuine clue from nature: the first detection of a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos at TeV-PeV energies opened neutrino astronomy as a new window on the extreme universe. The discovery is clear, original, and the instrument (a cubic-kilometre detector in Antarctic ice) was itself a bold concept.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and drove the IceCube concept, Karle led construction and detector-physics development, and Spiering was a leading figure in the neutrino-telescope programme and its results. This three-person configuration is plausible, but the many-hundred-member collaboration and the earlier Baikal and AMANDA pioneers make allocation delicate.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed: the diffuse flux has been verified with several independent analysis channels, and source evidence (the TXS 0506+056 blazar and NGC 1068, plus the Galactic plane) has followed. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Whether the supplied credited names fully capture the decisive contributors given the collaboration scale and predecessor experiments such as AMANDA and Baikal.
My recollection of the source-identification significance levels is from memory and not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, with the magic-wavelength idea, delivers fractional uncertainty near 1e-18 and underpins redefinition of the second, relativistic geodesy and tests of fundamental constants and possible dark-matter couplings. It is a clean, discriminating discovery-plus-invention with direct ties to gravity and cosmology-adjacent questions.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice scheme and demonstrated the first clocks; Ye brought the clock to record accuracy and coherence with strontium and pushed the precision frontier. Two laureates is a natural configuration, though Hall and Hansch (frequency combs) were already honoured in 2005, and ion-clock work by others is separate.
assessment.maturity: Mature: multiple independent labs worldwide operate lattice clocks, intercomparisons exist, and the stability results are well confirmed over more than a decade.
uncertainties: Overlap with the Nobel-recognised frequency-comb and ion-trap work could make some committee members regard the advance as incremental, which I cannot fully resolve.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theoretical prediction of flat bands at magic angles followed by the observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created the field of moiré quantum matter. It is original, clear and has already produced a wide range of confirmed phenomena.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the decisive theoretical prediction of the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group delivered the experimental discovery with Cao and collaborators. The experimental team includes junior researchers (such as Yuan Cao) who are not on the supplied list, which is a limit on fairness that I note rather than resolve.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many independent groups with consistent phase diagrams, though the microscopic pairing mechanism is still debated, which may argue for a little more time.
uncertainties: Credit for the experimental discovery involves junior authors outside the supplied credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators are a fundamental, lasting reorganisation of band theory, with the Kane-Mele proposal followed by experimental realisation. Their conceptual reach into topological materials is large, although the 2016 prize recognised related topological ideas.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the original theoretical proposal, and Molenkamp's group experimentally realised the quantum spin Hall state in HgTe wells following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang prediction. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and others (Fu, Moore, Hasan) contributed decisively but are outside this candidate's credited names, so the allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed across several material platforms and widely replicated over fifteen years; recognition is arguably ripe.
uncertainties: The decisive theory credit is shared with people not among the credited names (for example the HgTe prediction and three-dimensional extension).
Possible overlap with the 2016 topological-phase prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum cryptography links foundations (Bell nonlocality, no-cloning) to a practical technology with deployed networks and satellite demonstrations. The ideas are original and clear, and the experimental proof that nature permits this is a genuine clue from physics.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard introduced the BB84 protocol, and Ekert independently proposed the entanglement-based protocol, so this three-person configuration is natural and well supported. Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is a notable unresolved precedent.
assessment.maturity: Mature: decades of experiments, commercial systems and satellite links. The 2022 prize on entanglement experiments reduces room but does not duplicate this discovery.
uncertainties: Wiesner's earlier conjugate coding and the practical security of real devices may complicate how fundamental the committee considers this.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The baryon acoustic peak provides a standard ruler that independently measures cosmic expansion and underpins current dark-energy constraints. For me this is closest to the dark energy questions I work on: it is an observational clue rather than a model, and it constrains any string-theory or alternative account of acceleration.
assessment.attribution: The 2005 detections came from SDSS (Eisenstein) and 2dFGRS (Cole, Peacock), which makes the three-person configuration defensible, but the survey collaborations are large and the theoretical prediction came from earlier work (Peebles, Yu, Sunyaev, Zeldovich) that is not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed repeatedly (BOSS, eBOSS, DESI), though DESI hints of evolving dark energy are still developing. Cosmology has just been recognised in 2006, 2011 and 2019, so timing is plausible but not urgent.
uncertainties: Attribution between 2dFGRS and SDSS and the earlier theoretical predictions is unresolved.
Interpretation in terms of dark energy may shift with newer DESI results.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Transmission and emission spectroscopy of exoplanet atmospheres turned exoplanets from points into worlds with measurable composition and, now, with JWST biosignature-adjacent searches. The existential dimension appeals to me, though the 2019 prize already honoured exoplanet discovery.
assessment.attribution: Charbonneau made the first atmospheric detection (HD 209458b), Seager predicted the signatures, Deming made early secondary-eclipse and spectral work, and Snellen did high-resolution ground-based spectroscopy. Deming (early secondary-eclipse and spectral work) is left out of my three, and no set of three is obviously best, which reflects diffuse attribution.
assessment.maturity: Methods are validated by many independent observations, especially with HST and JWST, but the interpretation of particular atmospheres is still evolving.
uncertainties: Credit is diffuse among at least four people and a prior prize on the same broad topic may count against it.
The physics novelty versus astronomy classification is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first horizon-scale images of M87* and Sgr A* are direct evidence on strong-field gravity and the near-horizon structure of black holes, and they bear on horizonless-mimicker proposals I find interesting. The images are clear and visually compelling, but the physics tests are so far consistent with general relativity rather than revealing something new.
assessment.attribution: Doeleman led the EHT, Falcke proposed the shadow imaging concept, and Zensus led the VLBI technology and network contributions. In a collaboration of several hundred, attribution to three people is inherently arbitrary.
assessment.maturity: Two independent sources imaged and results are consistent, but the interpretation of polarisation and accretion models is still maturing, and Genzel and Ghez were honoured for black holes in 2020.
uncertainties: Collaboration scale makes fair attribution difficult.
The imaging result is a confirmation of expectation more than a new discovery, and its constraints on alternatives like mimickers remain weak.
